units.leftText: The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s. Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth;
units.rightText: This is Solomon’s Song of Songs. Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth!

units.leftText: Your oils have a pleasing fragrance. Take me away with you.
units.rightText: The fragrance of your perfume is pleasing; Take me away with you— let us hurry!

units.leftText: I am dark, but lovely, Don’t stare at me because I am dark,
units.rightText: I am dark, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, Do not stare because I am dark,

units.leftText: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, If you don’t know, most beautiful among women,
units.rightText: Tell me, O one I love, If you do not know, O fairest of women,

units.leftText: I have compared you, my love, Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings,
units.rightText: I compare you, my darling, Your cheeks are beautiful with ornaments,

units.leftText: We will make you earrings of gold, While the king sat at his table,
units.rightText: We will make you ornaments of gold, While the king was at his table,

units.leftText: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh, My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms
units.rightText: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms

units.leftText: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful, my beloved, yes, pleasant;
units.rightText: How beautiful you are, my darling! How handsome you are, my beloved!

units.leftText: I am a rose of Sharon, As a lily among thorns,
units.rightText: I am a rose of Sharon, Like a lily among the thorns

units.leftText: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, He brought me to the banquet hall.
units.rightText: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest He has brought me to the house of wine,

units.leftText: Strengthen me with raisins, His left hand is under my head.
units.rightText: Sustain me with raisins; His left hand is under my head,

units.leftText: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, The voice of my beloved!
units.rightText: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you Listen! My beloved approaches.

units.leftText: My beloved is like a roe or a young deer. My beloved spoke, and said to me,
units.rightText: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. My beloved calls to me,

units.leftText: For behold, the winter is past. The flowers appear on the earth.
units.rightText: For now the winter is past; The flowers have appeared in the countryside;

units.leftText: The fig tree ripens her green figs. My dove in the clefts of the rock,
units.rightText: The fig tree ripens its figs; O my dove in the clefts of the rock,

units.leftText: Catch for us the foxes, My beloved is mine, and I am his.
units.rightText: Catch for us the foxes— My beloved is mine and I am his;

units.leftText: By night on my bed, I will get up now, and go about the city;
units.rightText: On my bed at night I will arise now and go about the city,

units.leftText: The watchmen who go about the city found me; I had scarcely passed from them,
units.rightText: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city: I had just passed them when I found the one I love.

units.leftText: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, Who is this who comes up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke,
units.rightText: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you Who is this coming up from the wilderness

units.leftText: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage! They all handle the sword, and are expert in war.
units.rightText: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage, All are skilled with the sword,

units.leftText: King Solomon made himself a carriage He made its pillars of silver,
units.rightText: King Solomon has made his carriage He has made its posts of silver,

units.leftText: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Your teeth are like a newly shorn flock,
units.rightText: How beautiful you are, my darling— Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn sheep

units.leftText: Your lips are like scarlet thread. Your neck is like David’s tower built for an armory,
units.rightText: Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon, Your neck is like the tower of David,

units.leftText: Your two breasts are like two fawns Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away,
units.rightText: Your breasts are like two fawns, Before the day breaks and the shadows flee,

units.leftText: You are all beautiful, my love. Come with me from Lebanon, my bride,
units.rightText: You are altogether beautiful, my darling; Come with me from Lebanon, my bride,

units.leftText: You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride. How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride!
units.rightText: You have captured my heart, How delightful is your love,

units.leftText: Your lips, my bride, drip like the honeycomb. My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden;
units.rightText: Your lips, my bride, My sister, my bride, you are a garden locked up,

units.leftText: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits, spikenard and saffron,
units.rightText: Your branches are an orchard of pomegranates with nard and saffron, with calamus and cinnamon,

units.leftText: a fountain of gardens, Awake, north wind, and come, you south!
units.rightText: You are a garden spring, Awake, O north wind,

units.leftText: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I was asleep, but my heart was awake.
units.rightText: I have come to my garden, my sister, my bride; I sleep, but my heart is awake.

units.leftText: I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening.
units.rightText: I have taken off my robe — My beloved put his hand to the latch;

units.leftText: I rose up to open for my beloved. I opened to my beloved;
units.rightText: I rose up to open for my beloved. I opened for my beloved,

units.leftText: The watchmen who go about the city found me. I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem,
units.rightText: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city. O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you,

units.leftText: How is your beloved better than another beloved, My beloved is white and ruddy.
units.rightText: How is your beloved better than others, My beloved is dazzling and ruddy,

units.leftText: His head is like the purest gold. His eyes are like doves beside the water brooks,
units.rightText: His head is purest gold; His eyes are like doves

units.leftText: His cheeks are like a bed of spices with towers of perfumes. His hands are like rings of gold set with beryl.
units.rightText: His cheeks are like beds of spice, His arms are rods of gold

units.leftText: His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold. His mouth is sweetness;
units.rightText: His legs are pillars of marble His mouth is most sweet;

units.leftText: Where has your beloved gone, you fairest among women? My beloved has gone down to his garden,
units.rightText: Where has your beloved gone, My beloved has gone down to his garden,

units.leftText: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine. You are beautiful, my love, as Tirzah,
units.rightText: I belong to my beloved and he belongs to me; You are as beautiful, my darling, as Tirzah,

units.leftText: Turn away your eyes from me, Your teeth are like a flock of ewes,
units.rightText: Turn your eyes away from me, Your teeth are like a flock of sheep

units.leftText: Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil. There are sixty queens, eighty concubines,
units.rightText: Your brow behind your veil There are sixty queens and eighty concubines,

units.leftText: My dove, my perfect one, is unique. Who is she who looks out as the morning,
units.rightText: but my dove, my perfect one, is unique, Who is this who shines like the dawn,

units.leftText: I went down into the nut tree grove, Without realizing it,
units.rightText: I went down to the walnut grove Before I realized it, my desire had set me

units.leftText: How beautiful are your feet in sandals, prince’s daughter! Your body is like a round goblet,
units.rightText: How beautiful are your sandaled feet, Your navel is a rounded goblet;

units.leftText: Your two breasts are like two fawns, Your neck is like an ivory tower.
units.rightText: Your breasts are like two fawns, Your neck is like a tower

units.leftText: Your head on you is like Carmel. How beautiful and how pleasant you are,
units.rightText: Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel, How fair and pleasant you are,

units.leftText: This, your stature, is like a palm tree, I said, “I will climb up into the palm tree.
units.rightText: Your stature is like a palm tree; I said, “I will climb the palm tree;

units.leftText: Your mouth is like the best wine, I am my beloved’s.
units.rightText: and your mouth like the finest wine. I belong to my beloved,

units.leftText: Come, my beloved! Let’s go out into the field. Let’s go early up to the vineyards.
units.rightText: Come, my beloved, Let us go early to the vineyards

units.leftText: Oh that you were like my brother, I would lead you, bringing you into the house of my mother,
units.rightText: O that you were to me like a brother I would lead you and bring you

units.leftText: His left hand would be under my head. I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem,
units.rightText: His left hand is under my head, O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you:

units.leftText: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness, Set me as a seal on your heart,
units.rightText: Who is this coming up from the wilderness, Set me as a seal over your heart,

units.leftText: Many waters can’t quench love, We have a little sister.
units.rightText: Mighty waters cannot quench love; We have a little sister,

units.leftText: If she is a wall, I am a wall, and my breasts like towers,
units.rightText: If she is a wall, I am a wall,

units.leftText: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal Hamon. My own vineyard is before me.
units.rightText: Solomon had a vineyard in Baal-hamon. But my own vineyard is mine to give;

units.leftText: You who dwell in the gardens, with friends in attendance, Come away, my beloved!
units.rightText: You who dwell in the gardens, Come away, my beloved,
